title: Shopping in the city
paragraphs: My name is Nursultan Akhanov. I am nineteen years old and I come from Karagandy, in the centre of Kazakhstan. I study Economics at WKU — it is my second year and I enjoy it very much. Last Saturday, I decided to spend the day shopping in Uralsk. I had saved 15,000 tenge over the past three weeks — 5,000 from my monthly allowance, 7,000 from a part-time tutoring job, and 3,000 that my parents sent me for my birthday. I made a list of everything I needed and set off at ten o'clock in the morning.

My first stop was the central market, about fifteen minutes on foot from my dormitory. I needed fresh fruit and some dried goods for the week. The market was busy and colourful — sellers stood at their stalls calling out prices in Kazakh, Russian, and sometimes English. I bought one kilogram of apples for 800 tenge and a 500-gram bag of dried apricots for 1,200 tenge. The seller offered to give me a small bag of walnuts for free because I bought two things. It was a good start. Total spent at the market: 2,000 tenge.

After the market, I walked to a small bookshop on Abay Street. I had been looking for a book about behavioural economics for two months. The shop assistant — a friendly man in his fifties — showed me two options. The first was a hardcover edition with 450 pages. It was beautiful, but it cost 3,500 tenge. The second was a smaller paperback with the same content but only 280 pages — a summary version. It cost 1,800 tenge. I thought about it for a moment. The paperback was better value for a student on a budget. I chose the 1,800-tenge book and paid by card. The receipt showed the price, the date, and a short "thank you" message at the bottom.

My next stop was a mobile phone accessories shop, three doors down from the bookshop. My phone case had a crack in it and I needed a new one. The shop had about forty different cases — different colours, patterns, and materials. I found one that was exactly the right size for my phone model. It was a dark blue silicone case with a small WKU logo printed on the back. The price was 2,500 tenge. I asked the assistant if there were any cheaper options, and she showed me a plain black case for 1,700 tenge. But I preferred the blue one with the logo — so I paid the 2,500 tenge by card. Happy with my choice.

By lunchtime, I had spent 2,000 + 1,800 + 2,500 = 6,300 tenge. I sat down in a small café near the market to eat. The menu was written on a board above the counter. I ordered a bowl of lagman noodle soup for 650 tenge and a glass of compote for 300 tenge. Total for lunch: 950 tenge. While I ate, I opened my notebook and calculated my remaining budget: 15,000 − 6,300 − 950 = 7,750 tenge. Good — I still had enough for my most important purchase of the day.

My sister Aigerim was turning seventeen in two weeks, and I wanted to send her a birthday gift. I found a small gift shop near the café. The shop had scarves, notebooks, small paintings, and decorative items. I looked at a handmade scarf — soft, warm, and a beautiful deep red colour. The price tag said 4,200 tenge. It was more than I had planned to spend on a gift, but it was perfect for Aigerim — she loves red, and the winters in Karagandy are very cold. I bought it. Final calculation: 6,300 + 950 + 4,200 = 11,450 tenge spent. Remaining: 15,000 − 11,450 = 3,550 tenge. I walked home feeling satisfied — and already planning what to do with my 3,550 tenge next weekend.

dialogue.speaker: Altyn
dialogue.text: Nursultan! Did you go shopping on Saturday? You mentioned you had a big list.

dialogue.speaker: Nursultan
dialogue.text: Yes! I had 15,000 tenge saved and I spent the whole day in the city.

dialogue.speaker: Altyn
dialogue.text: 15,000 — that's a good budget! Did you find everything on your list?

dialogue.speaker: Nursultan
dialogue.text: Almost everything. I started at the market — apples for 800 and dried apricots for 1,200.

dialogue.speaker: Altyn
dialogue.text: And the bookshop — did you find the economics book you wanted?

dialogue.speaker: Nursultan
dialogue.text: Yes! But the hardcover was 3,500 — too expensive. I bought a paperback for 1,800 instead.

dialogue.speaker: Altyn
dialogue.text: Smart choice. And the phone case I saw you with — how much was that?

dialogue.speaker: Nursultan
dialogue.text: The blue WKU one? 2,500 tenge. I paid by card. I love it!

dialogue.speaker: Altyn
dialogue.text: So how much did you spend in total by lunchtime?

dialogue.speaker: Nursultan
dialogue.text: 6,300 tenge — and then 950 for lunch. I was calculating in my notebook!

dialogue.speaker: Altyn
dialogue.text: What was the big purchase at the end? You said something about a gift.

dialogue.speaker: Nursultan
dialogue.text: A scarf for my sister — 4,200 tenge. She turns seventeen soon. Worth every tenge!
